text: I did it from Germany and I can give you some general tips on leaving, although they might not be exactly tailored to your administrative situation. I quit my job, informed the authorities about when my unemployment would technically start and informed the agency for work that I was leaving the country. They processed all papers but noted that I was going to leave and therefore not receiving unemployment benefits, at least when abroad (can restart the claim if coming back though). Next, I informed my health insurance. I had purchased a long term travel insurance that I had to show them. I de-registered my address via mail (no in person appointments in Germany, I an certain in the Netherlands you can probably do this online??). I added the confirmation to my email to the health insurance. I closed all bank accounts except for one. In Israel, let your partner inquire with their health insurance whether they can co-insure you. I’ve read in this group that it’s possible with some insurances, but haven’t gotten to it myself yet since I do have the long term travel insurance. Other than that, I think the de-registration does the rest for you, in terms of other offices/authorities that might contact you. Those are the most important aspects I think, registration, health insurance, unemployment (all connected) and bank accounts.
